test_title: RRB NTPC - Graduate 2025 (CBT 2) Advanced Full Test - 03
subject: general
question: An inlet pipe can fill an empty tank in 4(1)/(2) hours while an outlet pipe drains a completely filled tank in 7(1)/(5) hours. The tank is initially empty. and the two pipes are alternately opened for an hour each, till the tank is completely filled, starting with the inlet pipe. In how many hours will the tank be completely filled?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Inlet (A)**: 4.5 hours | **Outlet (B)**: 7.2 hours. Let **Total Work** = 36 units.

**Efficiency**: A = +8, B = −5. In 1 cycle (2 hours), Net fill = 8 − 5 = 3 units.

Filling 36 − 8 (last stroke) = 28 units. 9 cycles fill 9 × 3 = 27 units in 18 hours.

Remaining 9 units: 19th hour (A) fills 8 units. Balance 1 unit filled by B in next hour? No, pipes are alternate. Last unit filled by A in 1/4 hour.

**Total time** = 18 + 2 (full cycle for 3 units) + part of last cycle → 20 hours and 45 mins.

**∴ The correct answer is 20(3)/(4) hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ In the first 2 hours (1 cycle), work done = 8 − 5 = 3 units.

⇒ To avoid overfilling, subtract peak efficiency from total: 36 − 8 = 28 units.

⇒ Number of 2-hour cycles to reach near 28 units = 9 cycles (9 × 3 = 27 units).

⇒ Time taken for 9 cycles = 9 × 2 = 18 hours.

⇒ 19th hour (Inlet A opens): 27 + 8 = 35 units filled.

⇒ 20th hour (Outlet B opens): 35 − 5 = 30 units filled.

⇒ Remaining work = 36 − 30 = 6 units. Inlet A opens again.

⇒ Time taken by A to fill 6 units = 6/8 = 3/4 hour.

⇒ Total time = 18 + 2 + 3/4 = 20(3)/(4) hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 20(3)/(4) hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Pipe Logic

When pipes work alternately, always calculate the net work per cycle. If an outlet pipe is involved, ensure the tank doesn't fill during the positive stroke before the cycle completes.

Negative Efficiency

Outlet pipes are treated as negative work. Efficiency = Total Capacity ÷ Time to empty.

Peak Filling Rule

The tank is considered full the moment the water level reaches the capacity, even if the next scheduled pipe is an outlet pipe.</p
